_doc: The weekly scout report: what exists out there that this box is not using. Written by the Claude routine described in docs/models.md and read by src/lib/model-scout.ts. Judgment lives here; facts about which model ids a vendor currently sells are NOT — those are pulled live from each vendor's model-list endpoint at read time, because a list committed to git is out of date the day after it is written. Fit verdicts are likewise computed at read time and never stored here: a verdict depends on what is running and how much disk is free, and both change hourly. They are now computed PER HOST — measured against the machine this console is running on, and against each other host's declared specs in config/hosts/*.json — so a claim in `why` or `notes` that a model does not fit needs to name which machine it means.
_schema: candidates[]: { id, name, kind: local|cloud, capability, why, checkpoint?, provider?, target?, mode?, params?, released?, license?, docs?, paper?, requirement? { vramGb, ramGb, diskGb, basis, estimated }, spec? { paramsB, precision, contextK, kind }, runtimes?, pricing? }. Give `requirement` when the authors published usable numbers; give `spec` otherwise and let estimateFromParams() do the arithmetic with an honest basis string. `runtimes` pins weights to one stack (e.g. ["metal"] for an MLX repo) and MUST be omitted for portable weights, which is most of them — absent means "runs anywhere", and GGUF counts as portable. Verdicts are computed per HOST: name which machine you mean in `why` and `notes`, because BeTenshi (31.8 GB VRAM + 63 GB host RAM) and B5 (one 128 GB unified pool) disagree about a good number of models. upgrades[]: { alias, from, to, why } — a like-for-like repoint of an alias already in ai-router.yaml.
generatedBy: weekly scout, 2026-10-12 — the week the ASR board changed what its own headline number means, and the week the Anthropic lineup moved out from under four of this router's aliases. THREE WEEKS, not one: the last report is dated 2026-09-21 and the last commit on main is 2026-09-23, so the routine missed two firings and three builds of movement arrived at once. Nothing in config/model-meta.json, config/ai-router.yaml or config/hosts/*.json has changed since 23-09, so NOTHING on this list was adopted and nothing was dropped for adoption. The Open ASR Leaderboard's 09-10 build added URGENT2024 (degraded/noisy speech) to the English average, which moved every tracked model's posted score by +1.4 to +2.1 WER without any model changing — and left eight models unmeasured on it, so the board's `avg` column is no longer comparable across rows. Re-ranked on the eight datasets common to both builds, nothing moved to three decimals; on the new noisy set, Cohere is open #1. The Open TTS Leaderboard's 09-10 build moved nothing this report tracks. Two earlier claims are corrected: last week's Anthropic and Gemini upgrade TARGETS have themselves been superseded, and docs/models.md's assertion that Hume's TADA is not on the hub is false — it has been there since January.

candidates.name: Cohere Transcribe (03-2026)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 12-10: model.safetensors 4,131,862,976 B plus tokenizer and config = 4,134,794,465 B for the whole repo. The repo's lastModified MOVED to 2026-10-07, so this was re-checked rather than assumed: the weights file is byte-for-byte identical, the whole-repo total is 456 B larger than the 21-09 read, and the licence tag (apache-2.0) and gate (`gated: auto`) are unchanged — a card or config edit, not new weights. HF reports safetensors dtype BF16 for all 2,065,804,048 params, which is exactly 2 bytes/param against that file size, so there is no codec or encoder outside the count. The commits endpoint is behind the gate and was not read, so WHAT changed on 07-10 is not claimed here. VRAM is 4.13 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only. Benchmarks are the Open ASR Leaderboard build dated 09-10-2026 — english_short_latest.csv at rev d3c0e9a, longform_latest.csv at rev 4f164c2, multilingual_*.csv at the revs listed in the Space's init.py — not from this box.

candidates.why: STILL THE PICK FOR BETENSHI, and this week the board gave it a fourth argument. BeTenshi has served stt from whisper-large-v3 on :8001 for the 49 days since this entry was raised on 24-08. The 09-10 build added URGENT2024 — degraded and noisy speech — and Cohere is open #1 on it at 9.50 WER against whisper's 13.73, a 31% relative error reduction on exactly the audio a microphone in a room produces. Only three models on the whole board beat it there and all three are proprietary APIs (zoom/scribe_v2_pro 7.99, assemblyai/universal-3-5-pro 9.08, elevenlabs/scribe_v2 9.20). That makes it open #1 on THREE of the four boards — long-form 9.73 vs whisper's 11.23 (next open model is parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 at 10.72), multilingual 3.84 vs 4.57, URGENT2024 9.50 vs 13.73 — and open #2 on clean short-form English at 4.67 vs whisper's 5.78, behind only Qwen3-ASR's 4.31. 923 RTFx against whisper's 470, for a 4.13 GB download. Its 14 declared languages include ARABIC, which this box has an evaluation harness for (config/arabic-eval.json, docs/arabic-model-experiment-2026-09-14.md) and which no other candidate here covers. UNREMARKABLE ON B5, which moved its stt to an 8-bit MLX Qwen3-ASR build on 20-09 and has the pool for anything on this list. The caveat is unchanged and is a click-through, not an application: `gated: auto` under apache-2.0, so a human accepts the terms once. 129,680 downloads in the last 30 days and 3,446,579 all-time.

candidates.name: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (transformers build)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 12-10 and byte-for-byte unchanged: model.safetensors 4,076,193,080 B plus tokenizer and config = 4,087,646,324 B for the whole repo. HF reports BF16 for all 2,038,052,480 params, exactly 2 bytes/param, so no hidden encoder or codec. Repo lastModified is still 2026-07-22. VRAM is 4.09 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only. B5 runs an 8-bit MLX build instead, roughly half this on disk — that figure has not been read off B5 and is not claimed here. Benchmarks are the 09-10-2026 board build.

candidates.why: THE SHORT-ENGLISH SPECIALIST FOR BETENSHI, and the entry the board's metric change hits hardest. In service on B5 since 20-09 as `qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit`, so this speaks only to BeTenshi, where :8001 is still whisper-large-v3. It is open #1 on clean short-form English at 4.31 average WER against whisper's 5.78, a 25% relative reduction, at 836 RTFx against 470. READ THE BOARD CAREFULLY THOUGH: its POSTED average on the 09-10 build is 5.75, which reads as fourth among open models behind microsoft/Phi-4-multimodal-instruct (5.02) and the granite-speech-3.3 pair (5.26, 5.36) — and that ordering is an artefact, because those three have NO URGENT2024 score and their posted average covers only the eight clean sets. On the eight datasets all four share, Qwen3-ASR is 4.31 and the other three are 5.02, 5.26 and 5.36. It leads them; the headline number says otherwise. Where it genuinely loses is coverage: multilingual 5.52 against whisper's 4.57 — worse than the model it would replace on four of the six measured European languages despite 30 advertised — and ABSENT from the long-form board entirely, so nothing is known about a meeting recording. On URGENT2024 it is 9.93, second-best open model, 0.43 behind Cohere. So Cohere remains the general pick and this is the narrow one: take it on BeTenshi only if that box transcribes short English utterances and nothing else, which is what voice input in the Studio is. Three weeks in service on B5 is evidence it runs, not evidence it is right for the other box. 346,284 downloads in the last 30 days, 780,754 all-time.

candidates.name: AuK-Flash (Tencent Hunyuan speech foundation model, distilled)
candidates.params: the Open TTS Leaderboard records 1.53B; HF publishes no count and the repo ships 6.76 GB, so the count is still not the footprint

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 12-10 and byte-for-byte unchanged: auk_flash.safetensors 6,122,209,092 B + vae.safetensors 637,322,604 B = 6,759,531,696 B of weights, 6,762,657,045 B for the whole repo; repo lastModified still 2026-09-09. HF publishes NO parameter count for either AuK repo and the safetensors index carries no dtype summary, so estimateFromParams() must not be used on them — the leaderboard's 1.53B against 6.76 GB of weights would be 4.4 bytes/param, so that figure describes one component. VRAM is 6.76 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured. Host RAM is the server process only: at 6.76 GB the weight set fits BeTenshi's card outright, so unlike the image models it needs no CPU offload and holds no standing host-RAM cost. Benchmarks are the Open TTS Leaderboard build dated 09-10-2026 (hf-audio/tts_leaderboard_results at rev dd84b35, read through the Space's own _refresh_leaderboard endpoint because the results dataset still returns 401 to an anonymous fetch).

candidates.why: THE SECOND CLONING VOICE, and the numbers are RE-VERIFIED on the new build rather than carried over. On CV3-Eval English in cloning mode — the one dataset and language where this model and the service actually running on :8004 are both scored — AuK-Flash is 3.35 WER / 72.67 SIM / 26.61 RTFx against ChatterboxMultilingualTTS's 4.43 / 53.13 / 0.99, identical to three decimals to the 18-09 read. That is +19.5 speaker-similarity points on the one axis a cloning service exists for, 24% lower word error, and 27x the throughput, under the same MIT licence. Confirmed this week from config/model-meta.json: local-chatterbox IS the Multilingual variant, so that is the right comparison and not the English-only ChatterboxTTS sibling. Across the whole CV3 English cloning board AuK and AuK-Flash hold the top two SIM scores of any model at 73.00 and 72.67, ahead of k2-fsa/OmniVoice (70.05, cc-by-nc), openbmb/VoxCPM2 (69.02) and Qwen3-TTS-Base (66.96). Take Flash and not the base: same 6.76 GB, 0.11 WER worse, 6x the speed. THE COST, stated plainly and unchanged: AuK-Flash declares zh and en only, where Chatterbox declares 23 including Arabic, and neither board measures Arabic at all. So this is an ADDITION for English and Chinese, not a repoint of :8004 — and a new service to write, because AuK is an instruction-driven pipeline that also does speech editing, enhancement and source separation, which nothing on either box can do. On BeTenshi 6.76 GB sits on the card beside Kokoro's 0.4 GB and Chatterbox's measured 3.0 GB without disturbing either; unremarkable on B5. Adoption is still thin and the report should keep saying so: 2,963 downloads in 30 days, 3,592 all-time.

candidates.name: Qwen3-TTS 12Hz (1.7B CustomVoice)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 12-10 and unchanged: model.safetensors 3,833,402,552 B (= 1,916,676,352 params x 2 bytes, and HF confirms dtype BF16) PLUS speech_tokenizer/model.safetensors 682,293,092 B, which the 1.7B in the name does not include — 4,520,218,951 B for the whole repo. VRAM is that x 1.15 runtime overhead. Not measured. Ignore the repo's `usedStorage` of 4,617,449,338 B; it counts revisions the download does not fetch. Benchmarks are the 09-10-2026 TTS build.

candidates.why: THE NON-ENGLISH READING VOICE FOR BETENSHI, unchanged and re-confirmed. In service on B5 since 20-09 as `qwen3-tts-1.7b-customvoice`, so this speaks only to BeTenshi. DO NOT REPOINT :8002 AT IT: on the English no-cloning board Kokoro-82M is 1.46 average WER at 71.15 RTFx against this model's 1.71 at 13.32, so for reading English aloud the 82M model already installed is faster, more intelligible and a fortieth of the size. WHAT SURVIVES IS BREADTH, and it is a real gap. Across all nine languages CV3-Eval measures, this model ranks 3rd at 4.22 average WER; Kokoro is unranked because it has no German, Korean or Russian at all, and the multilingual voice this box gained on 18-09 — Chatterbox — ranks 10th at 11.28. Per language, reading without cloning: German 5.96 against Chatterbox's 17.45, French 5.94 against 16.34, Russian 5.70 against 13.49, Japanese 5.90 against 8.82. All identical to the 18-09 build. So if BeTenshi needs to read non-English text aloud this is the model, it beats what shipped on 18-09 by two to three times on error, and B5 has already made that call for itself. The correction from last week stands and is re-confirmed on this build: the board records CustomVoice as NOT supporting voice cloning — 'CustomVoice' is a speaker bank. The `-Base` sibling is the cloner, 3rd on the CV3 English cloning board at 2.85 WER / 66.96 SIM. Downloads by metric, as docs/models.md requires: 2,224,976 in the last 30 days, 16,763,173 all-time.

candidates.name: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming 1.5B
candidates.params: 2.81B (the '1.5B' in the name is the LLM backbone only)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, re-read 12-10 and unchanged: model-0000{1,2,3}-of-00003.safetensors 2,498,354,152 + 2,486,576,066 + 643,458,072 B = 5.63 GB of weights, 5,645,212,528 B for the whole repo; lastModified still 2026-09-03. HF reports BF16 for all 2,814,116,321 params, exactly 2 bytes/param, so no separate codec outside the count. The name understates it: '1.5B' is the language backbone, the checkpoint is 2.81B. VRAM is 5.63 x 1.15 runtime overhead, not measured; host RAM is the server process only. ACCURACY IS UNMEASURED — see `why`; nothing in this entry is a benchmark claim about this checkpoint.

candidates.why: WEAKENED THIS WEEK, and the new evidence is worth stating before the case. This checkpoint is still ABSENT FROM ALL FOUR BOARDS on the 09-10 build, so its accuracy remains unmeasured — that was last week's correction and it stands. What is new is that the one measured member of its family just got a noise score, and it is the worst in its WER band: microsoft/VibeVoice-ASR-HF scores 19.50 on URGENT2024 against whisper's 13.73 and Cohere's 9.50, while sitting at 5.58 on the clean eight. A model that degrades that sharply on noisy audio is a specific doubt about this family for LIVE MICROPHONE transcription, which is the only job this entry is proposed for — so the case is now weaker than it read on 21-09, by evidence rather than by opinion. WHAT STILL STANDS: it is the only MIT-licensed model on this list that streams speaker-attributed transcription as audio arrives, and local-whisper on BeTenshi cannot show live text or tell two speakers apart at all. So: if STREAMING is the actual requirement, install it behind its own service and do not repoint the stt capability at it — the general route belongs to Cohere. If DIARISATION ALONE is the need, take OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize instead: it is measured (4.64 clean English, 12.74 URGENT2024, 9.08 multilingual), it is 0.91 GB against 5.65, and it is Apache-2.0 — better on every axis except the streaming itself. On BeTenshi 5.65 GB sits comfortably beside the speech services; the 7B sibling at 17.36 GB runs alone there and blocks every image model, and is unremarkable on B5, which is where the 7B goes if its accuracy is ever wanted. 6,106 downloads in 30 days, 12,839 all-time — still unproven.

candidates.name: Iris-3B (pixel-space diffusion + depth + upscaler)

requirement.basis: Disk EXACT from the repo listing, read 12-10, and the number is for the TEXT-TO-IMAGE MODEL ONLY: model.safetensors 11,950,112,680 B plus config.yaml, 11,950,126,805 B for the repo root. HF reports dtype F32 for all 2,987,511,888 params and 11,950,112,680 / 2,987,511,888 = 4.0000 bytes/param, so the release is fp32 and a bf16 build would be about 5.98 GB — none is published. THE WHOLE REPO IS 35.94 GB because `depth/` (11.99 GB) and `upscaler/` (11.99 GB) are two more complete fine-tunes of the same prior, so a naive snapshot download costs 3x what the image model needs; the README says so too ('about 12 GB for text-to-image'). VRAM is 11.95 x 1.15 runtime overhead with no CPU offload, since 11.95 GB fits BeTenshi's card whole; not measured, and NOT a peak — activation cost at 1 megapixel is unknown and pixel-space models carry more of it than latent ones. No benchmark figure is given because none exists: see `why`.

candidates.why: THE FIRST CLEAN-LICENSED ENTRANT THE IMAGE LANE HAS HAD IN A MONTH, and it is ranked on licence and capability, NOT on measured quality — there is no public image-generation board, nobody has A/B'd it, and docs/models.md says to say so rather than imply a number. WHAT IT BEATS HERE: local-flux-schnell, which is still in config/model-meta.json and was REJECTED by admission control on 12 September at 31.7 GB VRAM / 28 GB host RAM peak. Iris-3B is 11.95 GB of weights that fit the 5090 whole, with no CPU offload and therefore no standing host-RAM cost — roughly a third of schnell's footprint, and admissible where schnell is not. WHAT IT ADDS that neither box has: the same pixel-space prior, fine-tuned without architectural change, ships as monocular DEPTH ESTIMATION and image RESTORATION/UPSCALING in the same repo. Nothing on BeTenshi or B5 does depth or super-resolution at all, so this is a capability, not a swap — the same shape of argument Chatterbox was taken on in September. It also has no VAE: the network emits every pixel, which is the paper's claim for detail retention and is at least a different failure mode from the three latent models installed. THE HONEST COSTS. It is SEVEN DAYS OLD with 393 downloads, which is not evidence of anything either way, and the defaults are CFG 3 at 100 STEPS for a one-megapixel image — against Z-Image-Turbo, FLUX.2-klein-4B and HiDream-O1, which are few-step models at 12-22 GB estimated. Expect it to be slower per image than everything installed, by a factor nobody has measured. So this is an EVALUATE, not an adopt: apache-2.0, fits BeTenshi at 11.95 GB, unremarkable in B5's pool, and worth 12 GB of disk to find out whether the depth and upscaler heads earn their place. Download the root only; do not snapshot the repo.

upgrades.why: NEW THIS WEEK, NEVER RAISED BEFORE, and the only dated thing on this list. `claude-haiku` in ai-router.yaml points at anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5. Anthropic's deprecation page gives claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 a retirement commitment of 'Not sooner than October 15, 2026' — THREE DAYS FROM THIS REPORT — which is the earliest date of any model this router fronts, by more than a year. SAY WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN, because the gpt-5.5 entry already got burned on exactly this: the model is listed ACTIVE, it is NOT deprecated, and Anthropic promises at least 60 days' notice before retiring a publicly released model. So nothing breaks on Thursday. What passes on Thursday is the guaranteed-availability floor, after which a deprecation notice could arrive at any time, and this is the one alias in the file where that is true. claude-haiku-5-5 is Active with a floor of October 7, 2027. PREREQUISITE, and it is the same for the next three entries: claude-haiku-5-5 is NOT in ai-router.yaml. The last wire-all ran 2026-09-18 and this model's retirement floor implies a release around 2026-10-07, so discovery has not swept since it shipped. Run the console's Wire all first, then edit the alias — the wire is one click and one restart, the alias edit is one line by hand.

FIFTY-FOUR DAYS OUTSTANDING — first raised 2026-08-19, read from `git log --follow config/model-scout.json`, not incremented from last week's 'thirty-three days'. AND THE TARGET HAS CHANGED: this entry said claude-opus-5 for seven weeks and claude-opus-5 is now itself listed under 'Legacy models (still available)' on Anthropic's models overview. The current Opus is **claude-opus-5-5** at $4.00 / $20.00 per 1M input/output tokens. Retirement floors give the ordering and, minus one year, the ship dates: opus-5-5 not sooner than 2027-09-22, opus-5 2027-07-24, opus-4-8 2027-05-28 — so the wired model is two generations behind, and the target this report recommended last week is one. Those dates are DERIVED from the retirement commitment, not published release dates; the pattern matches what earlier runs recorded for opus-5 (2026-07-24) and opus-4-8 (2026-05-28) exactly. NO DEADLINE IS BEING CLAIMED: all three of opus-4-8, opus-5 and opus-5-5 are listed Active and none is deprecated, so this is a capability argument, not a retirement one. claude-opus-5-5 is NOT wired — unlike the situation last week, when claude-opus-5 already had its own alias from the 08-19 wire-all — so this now needs a wire-all before the alias edit.

FIFTY-FOUR DAYS OUTSTANDING, dated from git, and the same target correction as claude-opus: this entry said claude-sonnet-5, which is now Legacy. The current Sonnet is **claude-sonnet-5-5** at $2.00 / $10.00 per 1M tokens, with a retirement floor of 2027-09-28 implying a ship date around 2026-09-28 — ten days after the last wire-all, which is why it is not in ai-router.yaml. The wired claude-sonnet-4-6 dates from 2026-02-17, making this still the most stale alias in the file at just under eight months. Active, not deprecated; no deadline claimed. Needs a wire-all first, then the one-line edit.

FIFTY-FOUR DAYS OUTSTANDING, dated from git, AND LAST WEEK'S TARGET IS WITHDRAWN. This entry said to repoint at gemini-3.7-flash and asserted the id was 'known good' because the 08-19 wire-all had wired it. As of 12-10, **gemini-3.7-flash does not appear on Google's published model list at all**: the stable Flash line there is gemini-3.8-flash, gemini-3.6-flash and the lite variants, and 3.7 is in neither the stable nor the preview section. So the router currently carries a pinned alias to an id Google no longer publishes — which is a finding about the ROUTER, not just this recommendation. STATE THE LIMIT HONESTLY: this run had no GEMINI_API_KEY, so ListModels was NOT called and whether gemini-3.7-flash still SERVES despite being unlisted is not known here. The console's discovery half calls that endpoint every 15 minutes on the machine that has the key, and that is where the current answer lives — check the Models page before editing. The correct target is gemini-3.8-flash, which is NOT wired. gemini-3.6-flash, behind the alias today, is still listed stable, so nothing is broken; it is simply two Flash generations old. Do NOT repoint at gemini-flash-latest, which is also wired: see the note about pinning.

THIRTY-FIVE DAYS OUTSTANDING — first raised 2026-09-07, read from git. The price case was re-verified against OpenAI's published pricing page on 12-10 and holds exactly: gpt-5.5 is $5.00 / $30.00 per 1M input/output tokens, gpt-5.6-terra is $2.00 / $12.00 — a 2.5x cut on both sides of the meter. Last week's withdrawal of the 'no longer carried in the pricing table' claim also holds: gpt-5.5 is still listed, alongside gpt-5.5-pro at $30 / $180. The urgency is cost, not retirement. TERRA, AND NOW WITH A REASON TO REJECT THE OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVE: gpt-6-astra shipped 2026-08-27 and was wired on 18-09, and it prices at $10.00 / $50.00 — twice gpt-5.5's input and 1.67x its output. Repointing this alias there would RAISE the bill, so astra belongs behind its own name, which it has. sol is $4 / $20 and luna $0.20 / $1.20, so both change what the alias means; terra is the like-for-like. This is exactly the repoint docs/models.md says the console cannot make for you — familyKey() strips version tokens and cannot see that 'terra' is a tier name. All three 5.6 ids are already wired under their own names from the 08-19 wire-all, so this one needs NO wire: only the alias is stale.

FIFTY-FOUR DAYS OUTSTANDING, dated from git, and it finally has a PRICE behind it instead of a generation marker. OpenAI's pricing page, read 12-10, quotes transcription per minute of audio: gpt-transcribe $0.0045/min against gpt-4o-transcribe $0.006/min — a 25% cut for the newer model, with Whisper also at $0.006/min. Every earlier version of this entry rested on gpt-transcribe having dropped the 4o generation marker on 2026-07-27 the way gpt-image did, which is a naming observation and not an argument; the 25% is. gpt-transcribe is already wired under its own id, so this is an alias edit with no wire needed. gpt-live-transcribe is $0.017/min for streaming and the router's audio_transcription mode does not front it — the VibeVoice candidate above is the local answer to that gap and this repoint is the cloud half of the same problem. Note the page gives gpt-4o-transcribe token prices too ($2.50 / $10.00 per 1M) and gives none for gpt-transcribe, so the per-minute figures are the only like-for-like comparison available.

notes: NOTHING WAS ADOPTED, AND THE ROUTINE MISSED TWO FIRINGS. The last report is dated 2026-09-21 and the last commit on main is 7b24220 of 2026-09-23, so this is a 21-day gap on a 7-day schedule. Checked mechanically, per step 1b: no candidate's checkpoint appears in config/model-meta.json (which still holds the same fifteen local- ids), no upgrade's target appears in config/ai-router.yaml (all six aliases below are byte-for-byte where they were on 19 August), and config/hosts/b5.json still serves qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit and qwen3-tts-1.7b-customvoice as it did on 20-09. So nothing is dropped as adopted and nothing is newly in service on either box. The three-week gap is why this report carries three builds of board movement at once rather than one, and it is worth knowing that the schedule did not hold.

THE BIG CHANGE THIS WEEK IS THE BOARD, NOT THE MODELS. The Open ASR Leaderboard's 09-10-2026 build ('Add openai/gpt-transcribe. Add URGENT24 to avg English WER.') added URGENT2024 — degraded and noisy speech — to the short-form English average. Every tracked model's POSTED score jumped without any model changing: Qwen3-ASR 4.31 -> 5.75, Cohere 4.67 -> 6.26, whisper-large-v3 5.78 -> 7.84, VibeVoice-ASR-HF 5.58 -> 8.23. Re-ranked on the EIGHT datasets common to the 19-09 and 09-10 builds (AMI-Cleaned, Earnings22-Cleaned-AA-chunked, Gigaspeech-Cleaned, LS Clean, LS Other, SPGISpeech, Voice Arena Monsoon, Voxpopuli-AA-Cleaned), NOTHING MOVED to three decimals for any model this report tracks. AND THE BOARD'S `avg` COLUMN IS NOW A TRAP: eight rows have NO URGENT2024 score, so their average covers the clean eight only and flatters them against rows measured on the hard set. The three that matter are microsoft/Phi-4-multimodal-instruct (posted 5.02, MIT, 6B), ibm-granite/granite-speech-3.3-8b (5.26) and granite-speech-3.3-2b (5.36): they read as the top three open models on the posted board and they are 5.02, 5.26 and 5.36 on the clean eight, where Qwen3-ASR is 4.31 and Cohere 4.67. They do not lead. They are unmeasured on noise. Own the related miss too: all three were ALREADY on the 19-09 build this report claimed to have ranked, with identical scores, and none was mentioned — the same failure as last week's ARK-ASR and granite-4.1 omission. Also gone from the board: gladia/solaria-3 went 4.57 -> 18.90, which is a board-side change this report has no explanation for and does not affect any pick. Sixteen rows were dropped entirely, among them the AutoArk-AI ids that Edge0 now redirects.

THE WEEK'S MOST TEMPTING ASR MODEL, AND WHY IT IS NOT A CANDIDATE. TheStageAI/thewhisper-large-v3-turbo is new to the board (self-submitted 25-09 via huggingface/open_asr_leaderboard PR #118, recorded in the repo's own .eval_results/open_asr_leaderboard.yaml) and on paper it is the find of the month: cc-by-4.0, 808.9M params, 28 declared languages INCLUDING ARABIC, clean-eight English 4.54 — better than Cohere's 4.67 — and multilingual 3.61, the best of any open-weights model on that board. It is held out for TWO independent reasons, both verified from the repo rather than inferred. FIRST, THE VENDOR'S OWN TWO NUMBER SETS DISAGREE. The README publishes a table using 'the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard methodology' in which every elastic rung is WORSE than stock whisper-large-v3-turbo: mean WER S 6.12, M 5.90, L 5.88, XL 5.89 against Original 5.80, and multilingual S 4.36 ... XL 4.35 against Original 3.99. On the same named datasets the submitted run is 1 to 1.7 WER better than that table — LibriSpeech Clean 1.41 vs the README's 1.73-1.83, AMI 8.09 vs 9.14-9.60, GigaSpeech 7.89 vs 9.48-9.56 — so the submission used different decoding than the vendor's own benchmark page, in the direction that flatters it, and the README does not say which rung was submitted. SECOND, THE ACCELERATED ENGINES NEED A TOKEN. The only documented way to run the fast builds is TheStage's own SDK — `pip install 'thestage-elastic-models[nvidia]'` from a private JFrog index plus `thestage config set --access-token`, or the Apple SDK whose `initialize` 'is checked online' and 'Offline initialize fails'. That is an account dependency on a third party in the hot path, which is the opposite of what the :8001 service exists for, and it is not something a licence read fixes. FOOTPRINT, since it is instructive: the repo is 74.67 GB across 515 files because it ships prebuilt engines per GPU and per rung (models/GeForce-RTX-5090 7.40 GB, free/GeForce-RTX-5090 3.58 GB in S and XL, free/Thor 8.13 GB, H100/H200/A100/L40S/4090 directories, plus subscription/android and subscription/macos_ios behind a paywall). There IS a directory for exactly BeTenshi's card, and the root carries a plain fp32 model.safetensors of 3,235,581,408 B that LOOKS like a stock Whisper checkpoint — but whether stock transformers reproduces any published number from it is untested and is not claimed here. Worth a human fifteen minutes; not worth a recommendation.

ARABIC: THE MOST INTERESTING THING THIS WEEK THAT CANNOT BE RECOMMENDED. mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-Arabic appeared 2026-10-08 and is a streaming ASR model for MSA plus FIFTEEN named Arabic variants — Moroccan, Libyan, Tunisian, Algerian, Hassaniya, Gulf, Najdi, Omani, Sanaani, Egyptian, Sudanese, Mesopotamian, South and North Levantine, Chadian — built for code-switching, co-developed with Morocco's Ministere de la Transition Numerique as a sovereign AI asset. Mistral publishes 8.82% average CER across seven Arabic benchmarks at a 480 ms transcription delay, within 0.91 points of their own offline Voxtral Transcribe Arabic at 7.91%, with their normalisation code in the repo. That is the first time a major lab has shipped open Arabic dialect ASR with numbers, and this box has config/arabic-eval.json and docs/arabic-model-experiment-2026-09-14.md waiting for exactly it. IT HAS NO LICENCE. No `license:` tag, no `cardData.license`, no LICENSE file in the repo — only `base_model: mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602`, which is apache-2.0. Absent terms are at least as unread as `license: other`, so per docs/models.md it waits here until a human decides whether the base's Apache grant carries to a fine-tune published without one. FOOTPRINT, if the answer is yes: 4.43B params in BF16, and the real download is 8,859,446,848 B (8.86 GB) for model.safetensors — the repo totals 17.74 GB only because consolidated.safetensors is the SAME weights in mistral-common format. 8.86 GB x 1.15 is about 10.2 GB, which fits BeTenshi's card alongside the speech services, and is unremarkable on B5. Note the cost of the family on this box, though: Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602, the base, is 6.46 / 17.95 on the English boards — near the bottom on noise — so this is an Arabic specialist and nothing more. Also note it is absent from every Open ASR Leaderboard board, and its CER uses the authors' own normalisation, so it is a vendor number, not a third-party one.

THE IMAGE LANE HAS ONE CANDIDATE AND TWO NEAR-MISSES, and the licence is still what decides all three. Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo landed 09-10 and is the #2 trending model on the whole hub (556 likes): `license:other`, so out on unread terms exactly as the base Qwen-Image-2.1 is, and the footprint is the same shape — 32.49 GB for a '7.12B' model because text_encoder/model.safetensors alone is 17.53 GB. Ignore the third-party GGUF repacks that tag themselves apache-2.0; a repacker cannot relicense someone else's weights. inclusionAI/Ming-Image-0.1-Design is the painful one: MIT, confirmed in both the tag and a LICENSE file, 6.15B, built for UI, infographics, posters and text-rich design with RGBA transparent-background output — a capability neither box has and nothing installed approximates. It is out on BOTH machines for DIFFERENT reasons, which is why naming the box matters: the repo is 52.88 GB (8.6 bytes per declared parameter, because it ships an MLLM text encoder beside a 5-shard transformer), so on BeTenshi's 31.8 GB card it won't fit at any rung and the authors' own validated configuration is 'one CUDA GPU with 80 GiB VRAM'; on B5 the 128 GB pool swallows 52.88 GB without trouble and the inference path does not exist — `library_name: custom`, served through vLLM-Omni or the authors' Ming-Image repo, neither of which runs on Metal. Worth revisiting if a quantised or sharded build appears. krea/Krea-2-Turbo and Krea-2-Raw remain gated AND `other`; FLUX.1-dev is `other`. Nothing in text-to-image this week is both clean-licensed and demonstrably better than the Z-Image-Turbo / FLUX.2-klein-4B / HiDream-O1 trio installed and measured on 12 September — Iris-3B is clean-licensed and NOT demonstrably better, which is why its entry says evaluate rather than adopt.

TWO MACHINES, and this week the asymmetry is about stacks rather than sizes. Every speech candidate above is 4.09 to 6.76 GB with portable weights and no `runtimes` pin, so fit arithmetic separates nothing; Iris-3B at 11.95 GB fits BeTenshi's card whole and is unremarkable in B5's pool. WHAT SEPARATES THE BOXES IS STILL WHAT WAS INSTALLED, and it has not changed in three weeks: B5 moved its speech stack to Qwen3-ASR and Qwen3-TTS on 20-09; BeTenshi added a cloning voice on 18-09 and left its transcription on a model that is open #36 of 55 on clean English and 36th of 55 on noisy. So the recommendation still differs by machine: on BeTenshi, install Cohere Transcribe; on B5, there is nothing on this list worth doing. THE STACK-SHAPED REFUSALS this week are the interesting ones, and three of them would be missed by size alone. Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 (apache-2.0, 78.1B MoE, 78.85 GB) is refused on BeTenshi for size and on B5 for FORMAT: HF reports F8_E4M3 for 77.4B of its parameters, and B5's ladder is bf16 -> MLX 8 -> MLX 4 -> GGUF Q4/Q3/Q2 with no fp8 rung, so a repo that ships ONLY fp8 cannot execute there however the 128 GB pool reads — the opposite of the usual case, where B5 is the forgiving box. sm_120 executes fp8 natively, so on BeTenshi the format is fine and only the 78.85 GB refuses it. Edge0/Edge0-35B-A3B-preview is unchanged: apache-2.0, 19.73 GB, `library:mlx`, now explicitly 4-bit packed (U32 for all 34.66B params), so B5-only at any quantisation. FermionResearch/Phonon-2 is `library:mlx` likewise. The older size asymmetries still hold: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-7B at 17.36 GB runs alone on BeTenshi and blocks every image model; Voxtral-Small-24B, Ming-Image-0.1-Design at 52.88 GB, Qwen-Image-2.1 at 33.13 GB and Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo at 32.49 GB are all refused on BeTenshi and comfortable on B5 — where only the first of the four has a working stack.

THE PATTERN WORTH REMEMBERING, and the reason this report exists beside the Leaderboard tab: for anything that is not a plain LLM, the parameter count is not the footprint, and the gap is usually a text encoder, a codec, or a second copy of the same weights. This week adds four examples and two new shapes. Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo is '7.12B' and ships 32.49 GB (text encoder 17.53 GB). Ming-Image-0.1-Design is '6.15B' and ships 52.88 GB — 8.6 bytes per parameter. THE FIRST NEW SHAPE is Iris-3B: 2.99B at fp32, so 11.95 GB where a bf16 build would be 5.98, AND the repo is 35.94 GB because `depth/` and `upscaler/` are two more complete 11.99 GB fine-tunes of the same prior — a naive snapshot costs 3x the model you wanted. THE SECOND is Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-Arabic: 17.74 GB for 8.86 GB of weights, because consolidated.safetensors and model.safetensors are the same tensors in two formats. And TheStageAI/thewhisper-large-v3-turbo is the extreme case at 74.67 GB for an 0.81B model, because it ships prebuilt engines for seven GPUs and four compression rungs. The back catalogue: ResembleAI/chatterbox is 3.0 GB measured resident and 23.65 GB on disk (four t3 checkpoints plus both .pt and .safetensors copies of s3gen); LLaDA-Image is '6.54B' and ships 49.2 GB; FLUX.2-klein-4B is '3.88B' and ships 23.7 GB; Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B carries a 0.68 GB speech tokenizer the name omits; VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-1.5B is really 2.81B; AuK and AuK-Flash publish no parameter count at all. Every requirement in this report is built from the repo's actual file byte counts, all re-read on 12-10.

THIS WEEK'S LEADERBOARD TRAPS, all text, all unchanged or sharpened. prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf is still trending (2,634 likes, 4.55M downloads, apache-2.0) and its smallest build is still 5,946,648,928 B — 5.95 GB for a 27B model. precisionLadderFor() bottoms out at GGUF Q2, which prices a 27B near 7-8 GB, so the console quotes a rung this repo undercuts. Conservative rather than dangerous — a 27B fits BeTenshi at Q2 anyway — but the ladder has no ternary rung and should be expected to overstate anything from this family. Note the repo's usedStorage is 205.56 GB across all its builds, which is a download trap of its own. Edge0/Edge0-35B-A3B-preview remains the MLX trap. THE NEW ONE IS Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1, described under TWO MACHINES above: a repo that ships ONLY pre-quantised fp8 is a case the ladder does not model, because the ladder walks quantisations of an unquantised model and this one offers no rung to walk. Anything whose safetensors dtype map is fp8-only should be read as CUDA-with-fp8 or nothing. Also worth one line: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is still MIT and still 763B shipping 510 GB, and the Leaderboard refuses it correctly without help from this report.

What that cannot tell us is what each vendor's API actually serves to this key — in particular whether the unlisted gemini-3.7-flash still responds. The console's discovery half calls those endpoints every 15 minutes on the machine that has the keys, so check the Models page before editing an alias. ONE STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE, and it is the actionable part: FOUR of the six upgrade targets below are NOT in ai-router.yaml, because claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5 and gemini-3.8-flash all post-date the 2026-09-18 wire-all. So the first cloud action is not an alias edit, it is Wire all — one config write and one restart, which the console does from the page.

Both wired Gemini image models still report the 429 quota error recorded in model-meta.json. That is a billing state on the key, not a model choice — no scouting will fix it. Separately, gemini-pro stays pinned to gemini-3.1-pro-preview ON PURPOSE and that pin was re-verified this week: Google's model list still shows gemini-3.1-pro-preview as the newest Pro, still in Preview. Google publishes gemini-pro-latest as a moving alias and ai-router.yaml pins explicit versions so an archived result records which model produced it. Both -latest aliases are wired under their own names from the wire-all, which is fine; do not repoint a stable alias at one.

Text LLMs are deliberately absent from candidates. The Leaderboard tab ranks every open-weights text model with a published parameter count against the live card automatically, and cloud discovery carries live prices — a hand-written candidate there would go stale beside data that does not. This report's only contributions in the text lane are the gpt-5.5 upgrade above, which discovery cannot make because OpenAI's tier names look like ordinary words to familyKey(), the three Anthropic alias repoints, which discovery cannot make because familyKey() has no way to know that `claude-opus` is a stable alias rather than an id, and the traps above, which are the opposite case: models the automatic ranking will size confidently and wrongly.
